focus.label: Psoriatic arthritis with nail involvement
focus.why: node-3 shows DIP joint swelling with nail pustules/dystrophy, classic for psoriatic arthritis; node-2 antibiotics ineffective and use of retinoids/methotrexate supports immune-mediated mechanism, though worsening suggests refractory disease.

payload.analysis: Current evidence best supports psoriatic arthritis with nail involvement: DIP swelling, pustules, and dystrophic nails are classic, and the imaging finding of phalangeal erosions without right-hand involvement is consistent with an inflammatory erosive arthropathy rather than infection. Antibiotic failure plus response to retinoids/methotrexate further favors an immune-mediated process, though refractory course suggests possible resistant disease. Key items such as psoriasis history, specific nail signs, and inflammatory markers remain unretrieved, so diagnostic certainty is limited; still, all currently available information has been covered.

payload.query: Need detailed imaging of the hands/feet (X-ray or MRI) to assess DIP joint erosive changes, nail bed ultrasound or dermatology evaluation for psoriatic nail involvement, and laboratory tests including RF, anti-CCP, CRP/ESR, plus bacterial/fungal cultures to exclude infectious arthritis/osteomyelitis. These findings are core to confirm psoriatic arthritis and distinguish it from reactive or infectious alternatives.

payload.analysis: Combined with the suspected psoriatic arthritis with nail involvement, hand radiography reveals bone erosions in the left middle and ring finger phalangeal heads, supporting erosive arthritis. Negative bacterial culture and TB/hepatitis serologies argue against infectious and reactive causes, while retinoid/methotrexate history favors an immune-mediated process. Lack of RF/anti-CCP and MRI limits further differentiation, but all key available imaging information is covered and psoriatic arthritis remains most likely.

payload.report: Pustules under fingernails with swollen DIP joints and dystrophic nails suggest inflammatory erosive arthropathy. Hand radiography showing phalangeal erosions supports psoriatic arthritis with nail involvement. Negative cultures/serologies and antibiotic failure reduce infectious/reactive mimics. Retinoid/methotrexate use and worsening favor immune-mediated disease. Thus psoriatic arthritis with nail involvement is most likely; other hypotheses are less likely.
